entries.285399c0cae654a3: This reportable segment sells new aerial work platform vehicles and other vehicles, with net sales to external customers of ¥44,652 million for the fiscal year ended March 2026 (down 3% from the prior year) and gross profit of ¥7,607 million. The company manufactures hole-digging pole-erecting trucks, aerial work platforms, skid-steer loaders and other specialty vehicles and sells them in Japan and overseas. In China, consolidated subsidiary Zhejiang Aichi Gongcheng Jixie Co., Ltd. manufactures aerial work machines, and equity-method affiliate Hangzhou Aichi Gongcheng Cheliang Co., Ltd. manufactures specialty vehicles, including aerial work platforms; in New Zealand, consolidated subsidiary AICHI NZ LIMITED sells the company's products. The securities report gives the reason for the sales decline as mainly lower sales to the electric power industry. The securities report also notes that carryover sales arose in the first quarter of the prior year from the resolution of a chassis certification issue for truck-mounted aerial work platforms.

entries.3c6feb7f64b89321: Net sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥59,613 million, up ¥306 million (1%) from the previous year. Sales of specialty vehicles fell ¥1,374 million (3%) to ¥44,652 million, and sales of parts and repairs rose ¥1,372 million (11%) to ¥14,061 million. The Annual Securities Report states that the decline in specialty vehicle sales was mainly due to lower sales to the electric power industry, and the increase in parts and repairs was mainly due to higher repair sales.

entries.6eb276a7260272ef: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥7,511 million (up ¥71 million, or 1%, from the previous year), ordinary profit was ¥8,172 million (down ¥52 million, or 1%), and profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥6,658 million (up ¥323 million, or 5%). The Annual Securities Report states that operating profit increased as a result of continued productivity improvement and cost reduction activities. Non-operating income decreased ¥85 million (11%) to ¥700 million, which the Annual Securities Report attributes mainly to a decrease in equity-method investment income. Extraordinary income was ¥1,249 million, mainly due to an increase in gain on sale of investment securities. Gross profit was ¥7,607 million for specialty vehicles (down 12%) and ¥5,199 million for parts and repairs (up 18%).

entries.776d62d04cb29210: The [[term:annual-securities-report|Annual Securities Report]] states that the group (the company, 2 subsidiaries and 1 affiliate) manufactures and sells earth auger trucks and aerial work platforms for electric power, electrical and telecommunications construction, and aerial work platforms and similar vehicles for construction and cargo handling; manufactures and sells parts and repairs; manufactures and sells skid steer loaders and similar vehicles; and provides training on aerial work platforms. Net sales for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥59,613 million, of which specialty vehicles were ¥44,652 million, parts and repairs were ¥14,061 million, and other was ¥899 million. The Annual Securities Report states that most of the business relates to the manufacture and sale of aerial work platforms and to parts and repairs, that each accounts for more than 90% of total segment net sales and of total segment operating profit, and that its major customers are in the electrical and telecommunications construction and rental industries, on which it is highly dependent.
entries.7bb826ac77b0a9cd: This reportable segment provides after-sales services for aerial work platform vehicles and other products, mainly parts sales and repairs. Net sales to external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥14,061 million (up 11%), and gross profit was ¥5,199 million (up 18%). The company provides after-sales services, including parts sales and repairs, in Japan and overseas, and Zhejiang Aichi Gongcheng Jixie Co., Ltd., AICHI NZ LIMITED and Hangzhou Aichi Gongcheng Cheliang Co., Ltd. each provide parts sales, repairs and other services in their respective countries. The securities report states that the increase in net sales was mainly due to higher repair sales, and that the company pursued initiatives including one-stop service development, proposals for preventive maintenance and capturing vehicle inspection work.
